verdict_text: YES. The drop set `{2,5,8}` and the `kept`-order renumbering produce exactly the mapping the spec lists (3→2, 4→3, 6→4, 7→5, 9→6, 10→7, 11→8), writing into a fresh dict so no block can overwrite a survivor; the regex `h\.(\d+)\.(.+)` leaves `wte.weight`, `wpe.weight`, `ln_f.weight` and `ln_f.bias` untouched, and tensors are passed through unmodified so values, shapes and dtypes are preserved. Both required checks are enforced before any write — `layers == set(range(9))` covers "no block 9/10/11 remains" and "exactly 9 blocks remain", and `len(out) == 121` covers the tensor count — and an `AssertionError` exits non-zero with `out/T1/model.safetensors` never created. This assumes the helper `_ckpt.load_checkpoint` is a plain safetensors load that returns the tensors unaltered, which is not visible in the artifact shown.
